title: feat(plugin-audit, cli)!: hold the audit seal lock across an os migrate audit-* --apply run, and skip a sealer pass while it is held (P4b3)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DSbRjPgaUKFphhrvX2c6ZHi)_

Part of #31908 (slice P4b3; seat ruling 6885005594)
Blocked-by: #33489, #33637

Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — narrowed: `os migrate audit-key-material`, `os migrate audit-mail-bodies` and `os migrate audit-metadata-bodies` with `--apply` now refuse a run that rewrites an object declaring `lifecycle.seal` when that object's database offers no session lock (SQLite, Turso) unless `--sealer-stopped` is passed, and on Postgres or MySQL refuse when a sealer pass or another run still holds the audit seal lock after ten minutes; 18.4.0 ran both. `os migrate audit-side-copies`, new in this release, holds the lock and takes the flag from its first release. Widened: the `--sealer-stopped` flag, and new exports — `@objectstack/objectql` `acquireDatabaseSessionLock`, `tryDatabaseSessionLock`, `databaseSessionLockPgKey` and the types `DatabaseSessionLock`, `DatabaseSessionLockRunOptions`, `DatabaseSessionLockWait`; `@objectstack/plugin-audit` `holdAuditSealLock`, `AUDIT_SEAL_LOCK_NAME`, `AUDIT_SEAL_LOCK_WAIT_MS`, `STORED_METADATA_BODY_REWRITTEN_OBJECTS` and the types `AuditSealLockEngine`, `AuditSealLockFinish`, `AuditSealLockHold`.
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — `skills/**` teaches declaring `lifecycle.seal`, and no line there names an `os migrate audit-*` command, its flags, or the sealer's locks; the stale sealing lines in `skills/objectstack-data/rules/lifecycle.md` (one checkpoint per hour, no verifier) are follow-up #33773's, from P4b2.

**BREAKING** for an `os migrate audit-* --apply` run on a deployment where an app declared `lifecycle.seal`: on SQLite or Turso it now stops before writing anything and asks for `--sealer-stopped`; on Postgres or MySQL it waits for a sealer pass in flight and refuses after ten minutes. A run that rewrites no sealed object is unchanged on every database, and so is every dry run. No object declares `lifecycle.seal` by default (that is P4c), so nothing changes for a deployment that did not opt in. ADR-0087 disposition, in the changeset: `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`.

## Maintainer quick read

- **What changed:** the audit sealer and the four `os migrate audit-*` rewrites can no longer work on a sealed object at the same time. Each sealer pass also takes a database lock and skips the pass while a rewrite holds it; an `--apply` rewrite holds that lock for its whole run. Where the database has no such lock (SQLite), an `--apply` rewrite of a sealed object needs the new `--sealer-stopped` flag.
- **Why:** a sealer pass that sealed a row while a rewrite was redacting it would leave a checkpoint over the old value and the row holding the new one, so `os audit verify` would flag a sanctioned redaction as tampering. Seat ruling 6885005594 (options E + B) on #31908 picked this fix; ADR-0154 D3's amendment is #33489.
- **Risk and rollback:** it only matters for an app that declared `lifecycle.seal`. The insert path and the cluster lock `audit.sealer` are unchanged. The schema-migration lock now runs through the same shared lock code in `@objectstack/objectql`, with the same statements and messages (its existing pins are unchanged and green). Rolling back removes the lock and the flag; nothing stored changes shape.
- **Look first:** `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/seal-lock.ts` (`holdAuditSealLock`, B's refusal, `trySealPassLocks`), then `sealer.ts` (`runPass`: the skip, the release order, `PassLock.lapsed` before each checkpoint write), then `packages/objectql/src/database-session-lock.ts` (the extracted lock, and the session probe).
- **Two-minute check:** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/audit-seal/audit-seal-lock.test.ts`: expect every case to pass, including "waits out a sealer pass in flight" and the B group.
- **What you need to do:** nothing: #33489 and #33637 have merged, this PR's base is `main`, and the seat lands it once review passes.

## What changes

**E: the audit seal lock (ADR-0154 D3 as amended in #33489).**
- A second named database session lock, `objectstack:audit-seal`, beside the schema-migration lock. Both now ride on one extracted module, `packages/objectql/src/database-session-lock.ts`: a Postgres advisory lock or a MySQL `GET_LOCK` on a connection of its own outside the pool. The dialect statements live there once. `acquireSchemaMigrationLock` keeps its name, key, wait, statements and words; only its body moved.
- The module gains what the sealer needs and the migration lock never did: a try-once form that never waits and never prints (`tryDatabaseSessionLock`, answering the lock, `'held'` or `null`), and `isHeld()`, a probe on the lock's own session (a session that ended took the lock with it, so a failed probe reads `false`).
- **Where it is taken:** on the datasource that holds the audit rows, that is each sealed object's hot store (`engine.getDriverForObject(object)`). Where the hot store differs from the primary, the lock goes on the hot store. **One lock per database, not per datasource:** two datasources can reach one lock namespace (one Postgres database, or two schemas of one MySQL server, whose `GET_LOCK` names are server-wide). Each session a run or pass opens is marked with a second lock under a random name, taken before the named lock. A later session of the same run that finds the named lock held asks the database whether the session holding it there is the marked one (`pg_locks` in the current database; on MySQL, `IS_USED_LOCK` of the marker against the name). If it is, that lock already covers the database: the session is closed and nothing waits. A holder the run cannot prove its own is contention, as before (review 6894679963 M1).
- **The sealer:** each pass takes `audit.sealer` as before, then try-locks the audit seal lock on each sealed object's database. If another session holds it, the pass lets go of everything it took, writes nothing, and says so at `info` once an hour while it lasts. Both locks are held for the whole pass and let go when it ends. Before each checkpoint is written, the pass checks that `audit.sealer` and the seal lock of that object's database both still stand. A lapse of either fails the object's pass, as any lock lapse does (seat ruling 6884540128 item 2), and the seed it sealed is dropped.
- **The migrations:** `os migrate audit-key-material`, `audit-mail-bodies`, `audit-metadata-bodies` and `audit-side-copies` with `--apply` hold the lock from before their first rewrite to after their last, hot and archive runs included. Contended, they print one line and wait up to `AUDIT_SEAL_LOCK_WAIT_MS` (ten minutes, the schema-migration lock's wait), then refuse, having changed nothing. A run whose objects declare no `lifecycle.seal` takes no lock: no sealer pass reads its rows. Dry runs take none.
- Before any wait, the hold tries every database once. A sealed object on a database that offers no session lock is refused (B) before the run waits on another database (review 6894679963 N2).
- A run that finds its lock's session ended by the time it finishes says so at error, names `os audit verify`, and exits non-zero.

**B: where the database offers no session lock.** On SQLite, Turso and every other dialect, the lock answers `null`. There, an `--apply` run that rewrites an object declaring `lifecycle.seal` is refused before anything is written, naming the object and `--sealer-stopped`. With `--sealer-stopped` it goes ahead and prints one line saying it rests on the operator's word. The sealer takes no lock there and seals as before.

**`os migrate audit-side-copies`.** `main` brought this fourth ledger-copy rewrite (#33607) while this PR was open. D3 as amended holds the lock for every `os migrate audit-*` run, so it gets the same hold (on the copy tables it rewrites, which `--object` narrows), `--sealer-stopped`, and the non-zero exit on a lost lock. It is not in 18.4.0, so for it this is no narrowing: it ships with the hold.

**The lines an operator reads.** The wait, the timed-out refusal and the sealer's skip line name the four commands in full (one constant, `AUDIT_SEAL_LOCK_REWRITE_COMMANDS`), so `check:cli-command-ids` holds each name to a real command. The commands hand the hold a callback that calls `logger.warn(line)` rather than the bare channel (`check:logger-receiver-detach`).

**Not changed:** the cluster lock `audit.sealer`, the unique `(sealed_object, chain_key, sequence)` index, D7's amend-before-rewrite order, the dry-run default.

## Tests

Pins first, red before the fix (bfece9b2: the objectql primitive's file fails to load, and the sealer and hold pins fail on behaviour against a constants-only stub).

- `packages/objectql/src/database-session-lock.test.ts`: the key derivation (equal to the pinned schema-migration key), the try-once form on each dialect, a failed try handed on, the session probe, a lock of another name waiting and refusing in its caller's words; `ownLocks`: no marker without it (the schema-migration lock's statements unchanged), the marker taken before the lock, the Postgres check scoped to the current database and bound to both keys' halves, the MySQL check bound to the marker and the name, and a holder that is not the marked session read as contention.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/audit-seal-sealer.test.ts`, new describe: the pass holds the seal lock at every checkpoint write and lets it go; the hot store and not the primary; a pass skipped while another session holds it, said once, sealing on the first pass after; a session ended mid-pass stores nothing and drops the seed; no lock on a database that offers none.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/audit-seal-lock.test.ts`: the name, key and wait pinned; the hold on the hot store and not the primary; one lock per database; two datasources on one database (Postgres and MySQL) locked once with no wait and no line; a lost shared lock reported for every object it covered; the run's own lock on another database never read as cover (still waited for and refused); a sealer pass sealing both objects of two datasources on one database; a lockless database refused before any wait on another; none for a run with no sealed object; a failure to take it handed on; a lost session reported; a real sealer pass in flight waited out with the default wait; a timed-out wait refused; a sealer pass skipped while a run holds it; B refused without the flag, with a memory driver too, only for sealed objects, and going ahead with it.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/audit-redaction-seal.contract.test.ts`: each of the four commands declares `--sealer-stopped`, runs every rewrite under the hold on the objects it rewrites, and exits non-zero on a lost lock.
- The fake database in `seal-store.testkit.ts` (`sessionLockDatabase`) keeps session locks the way Postgres does, waits for real, and ends sessions, so the sealer and a hold contend on one database in-process.

Readings are under Verification below.

## Acceptance notes

- **The rulings' wording, as read here.** "`--apply` on any object declaring `lifecycle.seal` is refused": the whole run is refused before its first write when any object it rewrites is sealed and that object's database offers no lock. "Holds it for the whole run": the lock is held on the databases of the sealed objects the run rewrites; a run that rewrites none takes none, since no sealer pass reads those rows. Lapse: the sealer follows seat ruling 6884540128 item 2 (a lock lapse fails the pass); the migration checks its lock at the end and reports a lost one, because it cannot undo rows it already rewrote.
- **The wait's length (ruling item 6).** Ten minutes. A pass in step with the clock seals the one window newly due and re-counts the late horizon, a few hundred reads; a backlog pass is cut at 24 windows, and between two passes the lock is free. The value is pinned, and the staged test waits out a real sealer pass with the default wait.
- **MySQL's `GET_LOCK` names are server-wide**, so two databases on one MySQL server share the audit seal lock, as they already share the schema-migration lock. Across deployments, a rewrite on one makes the other's sealer skip passes while it runs. Not changed here. Within one run or pass, datasources on one server share one lock and never contend with each other (see What changes). On MySQL older than 5.7.5, which keeps one `GET_LOCK` per session, taking the named lock drops the marker, so such a run reads its own lock as contention, as before this fix. It fails closed and never runs unexcluded.
- **A side effect:** two replicas with no cluster service, whose `audit.sealer` lock is in-process only, now also keep their passes apart through the database lock on Postgres and MySQL. The in-process lock's info line says so.
- Shared package touched: `@objectstack/objectql` (`schema-migration-lock.ts` refactored onto the new module, new exports). No open PR touches `schema-migration-lock.ts`, the objectql barrel, the audit CLI commands or `audit-redaction-seal.ts`; `sealer.ts` was touched by #33637, which has merged; `origin/main` is merged in (fbdc0b8e7), and this PR's diff against `main` is P4b3 alone, 19 files.
